display.purpose: Extra-condensed 800. The open entry's name (caps) and its fit at 1280px and up; the page's one big number.

title.purpose: Extra-condensed 800 caps, set solid. Every page's h1; the open entry's name under 1280px.

head.purpose: Extra-condensed 800, sentence case. h2, dialog and sheet titles, the wordmark.

lead.purpose: 600. Email subjects, h3, campaign names, numbers on list lines.

body.purpose: Letters and prose within 68ch; input text on phones.

ui.purpose: Controls, table cells, entry names in bold.

meta.purpose: Italic. The second line of an entry, hints, dates.

micro.purpose: Key hints, footnote numerals, tooltips, menu shortcuts, chart axes.

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Overlays only: a slip of paper lying on the page. Shadow colour is black at 38% (90% at night).

motion.name: dur-state

motion.name: dur-file

motion.name: working

motion.name: dots

motion.name: row-new

narrative.overview: Before the web, salespeople found every business on a street in the criss-cross city directory. NearbyNudge prints a fresh one for each campaign: every business in range, set as a white-pages entry; what it says about itself, with its sources set as footnotes; beneath it, the letter worth sending. What this refuses is the SaaS dashboard made of soft cards, tinted panels and icon tiles.
keyCharacteristics: Two inks on white: black and edge red. The night version reverses them.
Every list is a directory. An entry is a white-pages line: name, dot leader, number.
Navigation is a thumb index. Views and sections are die-cut tabs. The open tab is red.
Sources are footnotes; checks are keys.
Corners are square, except where paper is die-cut (tabs) and where a circle means a dot.
One authored motion: filing. Everything else that moves only shows a state.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Black and edge red on white, reversed at night. A new colour needs a new meaning, and there isn't one.

rules.name: The No Grey Text Rule
rules.body: ink-soft is for placeholders, disabled labels and facts the reviewer marked wrong. Anything else that wants to be quieter is set in italic.

rules.name: The Edge Halftone Rule
rules.body: Edge red may be screened only for something passing: text selection (24% edge on paper) and the fade on a row that just arrived (14%, gone in 1.4s). It never rests as a background; there is no pink wash.

rules.name: The Solid Caps Rule
rules.body: Caps are only ever the heading itself, set solid (0.004em). They are never a tracked-out label above a heading.

rules.name: The Fit Weight Rule
rules.body: A fit number's weight says how strong it is, everywhere: Strong 800, Good 600, Weak 400. The word carries the meaning; the weight echoes it.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page itself casts a shadow. Grouping is done with rules: 3px for running heads and notices, 2px for sections and frames, 1px for boxes and columns, hairlines between rows.

dos: Do set every list as white-pages lines: bold name, dot leader, condensed tabular number, italic aside beneath.
Do keep edge red (#C8102E, #FF5C61 at night) for here and needs you, and nothing else.
Do pair every drawn mark, meter and fill with a word, so colour and shape are never the only signal.
Do give each screen one bold element besides the running head and the thumb index.
Do separate with rules (3px, 2px, 1px, hairline) instead of boxes, fills or shadows.
Do keep every touch target at least 44px on phones and every focus ring a 2px ink outline.
donts: Don't set text in grey; use italic for what is secondary.
Don't put soft cards, tinted panels, icon tiles or a pink wash on the page.
Don't round a corner other than a die-cut tab or a radio.
Don't set a tracked-out caps label above a heading.
Don't separate meta with middle dots or put arrows on links and buttons; full stops and commas do that job.
Don't add motion beyond filing and the three state signals, and never let anything move under reduced motion or paused live updates.
